title: Mapping and transformation, and where secrets live

concept.heading: A mapping is a pure function with a golden example
paragraphs: The payment processor sends a webhook event shaped the processor's way: nested objects, cents, lowercase currency, an epoch timestamp. The CRM wants a flat donation record shaped its way. In Make this is the mapping panel; in code it is one function, webhook_to_donation(event), that takes the event dict and returns a DonationRecord.

Pure means the function depends only on its input. That is what makes it testable with a golden case: the exact event the processor sent last week, and the exact record it must become. When the processor renames a field, the golden test fails before a bad record reaches the CRM.

This lesson also introduces configuration. The CRM key comes from the environment through a git-ignored .env file, read once by load_config(). It is never a default in code, never in a log line, never in a test fixture. The check proves it by capturing every log line and grepping for the key.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: The mapping panel of a Make scenario or the Compose and Parse JSON actions in Power Automate, plus the connection reference that held the key. The connection reference becomes an environment variable.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: dicts, comprehensions, dataclass vs pydantic, .env
pythonBlock.intro: Nested dict access with .get() avoids KeyError on optional fields. pydantic (not dataclass) is used here because it validates; dataclass only stores.
pythonBlock.code:
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()                      # reads .env into os.environ, once
key = os.environ.get('CRM_API_KEY')  # None when missing -> raise ValueError('CRM_API_KEY ...')

charge = event['data']['object']
campaign = charge.get('metadata', {}).get('campaign')   # None when absent
emails = [d['email'].strip().lower() for d in donors]    # a comprehension
when = datetime.fromtimestamp(event['created'], tz=timezone.utc)
stamp = when.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')

spec: Copy .env.example to .env and set CRM_API_KEY to any value. Confirm .env is git-ignored (git status must not list it).
Implement load_config(dotenv_path=None): load .env (or the given path), build Config from CRM_URL and CRM_API_KEY, raise ValueError naming CRM_API_KEY when it is missing.
Implement webhook_to_donation(event) per the field rules in the DonationRecord docstring; raise UnsupportedEvent for anything but charge.succeeded.
Log exactly one INFO line per event ('transformed <event id> -> <charge id>') and never log any config value.
Compare your output against checks/m0/golden/expected_records.json before running the check.
askClaudeFor: A review of the method mapping (ach_debit -> ach, card -> card, check -> check) for anything you missed.
How caplog works in pytest, so you understand what the secret-in-logs test is doing.
writeYourself: The whole webhook_to_donation function, field by field.

check.command: uv run --directory middleware python checks/run.py m0-3-mapping-transform
check.summary: Golden input produces golden output for two events, a refund raises UnsupportedEvent, config loads from the environment, and the secret is absent from captured logs.
